display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 320px; text-align: center; width: 320px;

span.p:
Eviction behavior:
- When a slab class is full, the LRU tail of THAT class is evicted
- A write of 50 bytes evicts from slab class 1 only
- A write of 200 bytes evicts from slab class 3 only
- Big items cannot evict many small items (critical for fairness)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 320px; text-align: center; width: 320px;

span.p:
Problem: slab class imbalance.
If most writes are 200 bytes, slab class 3 fills up and evicts
frequently. Slab class 1 (64 bytes) may have free space but
cannot be used by 200-byte items.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 320px; text-align: center; width: 320px;

span.p:
Solution: slab rebalancing (Memcached 1.5+). Moves pages from
underutilized slab classes to overutilized ones.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 320px; text-align: center; width: 320px;

span.p:
Memory is divided into slab classes, each holding items of a
specific size range. Each slab class has its own LRU list.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Slab Class 1 (64 bytes/chunk) LRU: [A, B, C, D, ...]
